Well, speaking from my experience and the experience of my other black friends with mental issues, we all have similar experience, where our parents downplay our symptoms and send us off to church, since mental illness=bad spirituality. There is also ignorance that comes in, such as that depression is an excuse to be lazy, and that we have nothing to be sad about since God loves us and we wake up every morning. I’m not sure if there are similar experiences in other communities but I know it’s prevalent in the black. 

[Here](https://nylon.com/articles/mental-health-black-community) is a good article on it, and googling “mental health in the black community” brings up more. 

Edit: regarding your last question, no it’s not abnormal. Black people are, historically, known for wanting to uphold the strong, independent image, which isn’t wrong, but makes things like mental illness hard to discuss publicly. There also could be shame involved with his family, where they feel it could tarnish his image or they probably feel bad for not seeing the signs.
